metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.shortDescription: How often you get answers correct
metrics.longDescription: The percentage of questions you answer correctly across all quizzes and exams. This is one of the most direct measures of your subject understanding.
metrics.calculation: (Number of correct answers / Total questions) x 100

interpretation.high: Outstanding! You have strong command of the material.
interpretation.medium: Solid understanding. Focus on problem areas to improve further.
interpretation.low: Review fundamentals. Master basic concepts before advancing.

metrics.example: Answering 18 out of 20 questions correctly = 90% accuracy.
howToImprove: Review study materials before taking quizzes
Take notes while studying and review them
Practice with flashcards on weak topics
Ask teachers for clarification on confusing concepts

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.shortDescription: How regular and steady your study habits are
metrics.longDescription: Measures how stable and predictable your performance is across different study sessions. High consistency means you perform similarly well each time.
metrics.calculation: Based on the standard deviation of your quiz scores. Lower variation in scores means higher consistency.

interpretation.high: Excellent! You maintain steady performance. Your study habits are working well.
interpretation.medium: Good, but there are some ups and downs. Try to study at the same time each day.
interpretation.low: Your scores vary a lot. Set a regular study schedule to build consistency.

metrics.example: Student A: 70%, 72%, 71% = High consistency. Student B: 45%, 85%, 60% = Low consistency.
howToImprove: Set a fixed daily study time (e.g., 7 PM every night)
Create a quiet, distraction-free study space
Take short breaks every 25-30 minutes
Review notes before each study session

metrics.name: Response Speed
metrics.shortDescription: Average time to answer each question
metrics.longDescription: The average time you take to answer each question. Faster does not always mean better - balance speed with accuracy.
metrics.calculation: Total quiz time / Number of questions answered

interpretation.high: Very fast! Make sure you are not rushing through questions.
interpretation.medium: Good pace. You are thinking through answers appropriately.
interpretation.low: Taking too long. Review material before quizzing.

metrics.example: Completing 20 questions in 8 minutes = 24 seconds per question.
howToImprove: Take practice quizzes under timed conditions
Skip difficult questions and come back later
Read questions carefully but avoid overthinking
Study more to reduce hesitation on answers

metrics.name: Completion Rate
metrics.shortDescription: How many quizzes you finish once started
metrics.longDescription: The percentage of quizzes you complete after starting them. Abandoning quizzes means missed learning opportunities.

interpretation.high: Excellent commitment! You see things through.
interpretation.medium: Good but sometimes abandon quizzes. Push through difficult questions.
interpretation.low: Often leave quizzes unfinished. Try shorter quizzes first.

metrics.example: Starting 10 quizzes and finishing 9 = 90% completion rate.
howToImprove: Start with shorter quizzes (5-10 questions)
Set a goal to finish every quiz you start
Take a break if frustrated, then return
Remember: incomplete quizzes do not help learning

metrics.name: Mastery
metrics.longDescription: A weighted average of your performance. Harder questions count more toward your mastery score.
metrics.calculation: Weighted average where hard questions count 3x, medium 2x, easy 1x

interpretation.high: Ready for exams! Focus on review and advanced topics.
interpretation.low: Building foundation. Master basics before moving on.

metrics.example: Scoring well on hard questions increases mastery faster than easy ones.
howToImprove: Master easy topics first, then tackle hard ones
Use spaced repetition for better retention
Teach concepts to someone else
Take practice exams under real conditions

metrics.name: Improvement Rate
metrics.shortDescription: How much your scores increase daily
metrics.longDescription: The average daily change in your quiz scores. Positive numbers mean you are getting better!
metrics.calculation: Average daily score improvement over the last 7 days

interpretation.high: Excellent growth! You are learning efficiently.
interpretation.low: Slower improvement. Try different study methods.

metrics.example: Score 60% today and 64% tomorrow = 4% improvement rate.
howToImprove: Track your weak areas and focus on them
Study in shorter, more frequent sessions
Use active recall instead of passive reading
Get feedback on your mistakes

metrics.name: Risk Level
metrics.longDescription: A combined score predicting your chance of falling behind if no action is taken. Lower is better.
metrics.calculation: Combines consistency (30%), accuracy (20%), mastery (30%), and completion (20%)

interpretation.high: Low risk. You are on the right track!
interpretation.medium: Medium risk. Pay attention to weak areas.

metrics.example: Low consistency + low accuracy + low mastery = High risk.
howToImprove: Address low-scoring metrics first
Create a weekly study schedule
Set small, achievable daily goals
Ask for help when stuck
